newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Fenosa Jan to April net profit up 1.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Fenosa Jan to April net profit up 1.8 pct.

text.p: Spanish electricity firm Union Fenosa said on Friday its net profit in the four months to end-April rose 1.8 percent, and year-end results are seen in line with this increase.
No-one at Fenosa was available to clarify whether the figure referred to the group or to the parent company.

In a statement released ahead of the annual shareholder's meeting, the firm said: "Profits after tax in the first four months of the year rose 1.8 percent, a rise which will set the trend seen at the end of the year."

In an address to shareholders, deputy chairman and chief executive officer Victoriano Reinoso said: "The current year will be a difficult one in which we have to take on a substantial decrease in the tariff."

Chairman Jose Maria Amusategui said an expected increase in economic activity, falls in financial costs and exchange rate stability would nevertheless benefit the firm, whose position has been reinforced by new regulations governing the sector.
"The new regulatory model...gives incentives for coal use which favours the function of fossil-fuel plants," he said.
He added that future strategy would focus on efficient management of electricity and, secondly, expansion into new markets and business activities.
Shareholders approved an eight percent dividend increase paid against 1996 results, for a gross payment of 54 pesetas per share.
